newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mandela's sweetheart Machel won't seek top UN post.
newsitem.headline: Mandela's sweetheart Machel won't seek top UN post.

text.p: Mozambique's former first lady Graca Machel has no plans to run for the post of United Nations Secretary-General as an alternative to disputed incumbent Boutros Boutros-Ghali, officials said on Friday.
Reports circulated earlier this week that the widow of Mozambique's independence leader Samora Machel -- now romantically linked to South African President Nelson Mandela -- might be a candidate.
But President Joaquim Chissano's press attache, Antonio Matonse, said Graca Machel had informed Chissano she would not seek the world body's top post.
The United States on Monday vetoed Boutros-Ghali's bid for a second five-year term, blocking the wishes of its 14 fellow members on the U.N. Security Council.
The move effectively opened a race for the post, but Boutros-Ghali's candidacy still has strong support outside Washington.

Matonse said Machel "explained to the President that several diplomats had contacted our offices in the United Nations proposing that she be a candidate. Our offices at the UN informed her of that and her answer was a refusal."

"At the same time, various international personalities talked to the head of state about the same idea. Later, Mrs Machel phoned the President to explain the situation and reiterate that she is not interested in occupying the present post of Boutros-Ghali."
Machel is currently travelling abroad and was not available for comment.

The widow of Mozambique's first president, who died in 1986, revealed earlier this year she is involved in a romantic relationship with 78-year-old Mandela. The pair spend two weeks each month together but say they have no plans to marry.
Machel, 51, was appointed by Boutros-Ghali, at the request of the U.N. general assembly, to chair the U.N. Study of the Impact of Armed Conflict on Children.
In 1995 she won the U.N. Nansen Medal for "outstanding contributions on behalf of refugee children".
Mozambique has subscribed to the collective decision of the Organisation of African Unity to support the re-election of Boutros-Ghali, an Egyptian.
